narrative.overview:
Love Inc LMS is built like a register — a living, named record of a discipleship community. Every element earns its place by doing a job. The system is confident without being loud, warm without being soft. The brand's bold condensed wordmark sets the tone: this isn't a generic tool. It belongs to real people at real universities who are serious about what they're doing together.

The palette is built on restraint. A single accent — Fellowship Burgundy — carries the entire brand weight. It appears on the wordmark, on active navigation, on the confirmation of an action. Everywhere else, near-black and gray do the structural work. The result is a system where the burgundy always means something.

The interface rejects the aesthetics of both the corporate LMS and the faith-tech startup. Love Inc is a specific community at specific universities. The design is specific to them.
keyCharacteristics: Single accent system: Fellowship Burgundy on ink-black and page-white infrastructure
Flat by default — tonal contrast, no shadows
Typography-first hierarchy: weight and size, never color for emphasis
Structural confidence from the Helvetica Neue foundation
Community photos as content, not decoration

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Fellowship Burgundy appears in at most three roles on any given screen: wordmark, active navigation, and one interactive confirmation. Its rarity is the point. If it appears more than three times, rethink the layout.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: There are no shadows. Depth is conveyed entirely through tonal contrast: Ink Black topbar, Archive Gray sidebar, Page White content. Never introduce a box-shadow to solve a layering problem — solve it with background color.

rules.name: The Weight Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is size and weight, never color. A heading does not become Fellowship Burgundy for emphasis — it becomes 500 weight and larger size. Color emphasis belongs exclusively to interactive and brand states.

rules.name: The Single Family Rule
rules.body: One typeface. No serifs, no display-only variants, no pairing experiments. Helvetica Neue at two weights is sufficient.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow at rest, hover, active, or focus. If a component needs to feel interactive, change its border color — Rule Line to Fellowship Burgundy for focus, Rule Line to Field Gray for hover. Never add a shadow.

dos: Do use Fellowship Burgundy exclusively for: wordmark 'Inc', active navigation states, input focus borders, avatar backgrounds, and text links.
Do convey depth through tonal background layering — Ink Black topbar, Archive Gray sidebar, Page White content — not shadows.
Do use Helvetica Neue at 500 weight and larger size for all heading hierarchy.
Do place community photos at full width or anchored in a defined content zone — they are content.
Do render the wordmark as 'Love' in one color + 'Inc' in Fellowship Burgundy, in a single sans-serif weight.
Do use uppercase + letter-spacing exclusively for structural labels. Never for body copy or page headings.
Do express active navigation state through Page White background + 500 weight text. No side-stripe border.
donts: Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe. Remove existing side-stripes from sidebar active state and assignment list items.
Don't use soft gradients, stock photography, or generic religious imagery.
Don't build screens that look like Canvas or Blackboard — collapsible module accordions, institutional blue-gray palettes, progress bars as primary UI.
Don't use corporate HR or onboarding patterns: completion percentages, achievement badges, gamified streaks.
Don't use box-shadow anywhere. Change border color instead.
Don't add a second accent color. If the interface feels too gray, use larger typography and more confident spacing.
Don't color a heading or body text with Fellowship Burgundy for emphasis. Weight and size are the emphasis tools.
Don't use gradient text or background-clip text effects.
